1  THIS MFA IS FILED U/S.173(1) OF MV ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 17.08.2021 PASSED IN MVC NO. 1113/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND CJM., AND MEMBER, ADDITIONAL M.A.C.T.,
HASSAN, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL IS COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 17.08.2021 passed in MVC.No.1113/2016 by Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM at Hassan, (for short the 'Tribunal') the present appeal is filed by the petitioner therein for enhancement of compensation awarded.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that, on 24.12.2013 at about 7.00 p.m., the petitioner was walking along with his uncle on the left side of the road, a tractor bearing No.KA-13-T- 6611 came from back side in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and as a result the petitioner sustained with grievous injuries.
i. Two fractures of maxilla on both side.
ii. Nasal bone fracture of maxilla on both sides.
iii. Fracture of mandible involving left parasynthys region.

iv. Laceration over the cheek.
 v. Avulsion of multiple teeth and degloveing  injury of mandible.
4.

The Tribunal based on the evidence let-in came to the conclusion that the accident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the tractor which was duly insured with respondent No.2 and respondent No.2 is liable to pay a sum of Rs.11,53,888/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum under the following heads:
 SL. AMOUNT IN  HEADS OF COMPENSATION  NO. RS.
 1. Towards pain and agony 1,50,000.00
2 . Loss of amenities 1,50,000.00

3. Medical expenses 1,10,000.00 Prashantha vs The Manager on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8240350/
2  4. Loss of income during laid up 13,000.00  period  5. Rest, nourishment and 1,650.00  attendants charges  6. Loss of future income 7,29,238.00  Total 11,53,888.00
5. Not satisfied by the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
6. The accident occurred in the year 2013.
The income of the petitioner has not been established before the Tribunal.
Hence, the notional income as prescribed in the Lok-Adalath chart has to be considered, which will be Rs.8,000/- per month.
Further, the doctor, who has examined him has opined that there is disability to a tune of 64.5%.
However, the Tribunal has considered the total body disability at 51.94%.
However, given the nature of injury and description, I am of the opinion that the total body disability taken by the Tribunal is just and fair.
The petitioner was aged 16 years at the time of accident.

Hence, the multiplier of '18' has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. D.T.C [2009(6) SCC 121], thus the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.8,97,523/- (Rs.8,000x12x18x51.94%) towards 'loss of future income' as against Rs.7,29,238/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Given the nature of injuries, the laid up period has to be considered as 2 months and loss of income during laid up period will be Rs.16,000/-(Rs.8,000x2) as against Rs.13,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Towards the head 'pain and suffering', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,50,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards 'loss of amenities', a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards the head 'Medical expenses' based on the actual bills, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,10,000/-, which I deem to be appropriate.
Towards rest, nourishment and attendants charges, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,650/-.

Given the nature of injuries, the same is enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.
7.
Thus, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.11,53,888/- as described in the table below:

COMPENSATION COMPENSATION  HEADS OF AWARDED BEFORE AWARDED BY SL.
 COMPENSATION TRIBUNAL THIS COURT NO.

(AMOUNT IN RS.) (AMOUNT IN  RS.)
1. Towards pain and agony 1,50,000.00 1,50,000.00 2.
Medical expenses 1,10,000.00 1,10,000.00 4. Loss of income during 13,000.00 16,000.00  laid up period 5. Rest, nourishment and 1,650.00 10,000.00
attendants charges 6. Loss of future income 7,29,238.00 8,97,523.00

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.13,33,523/- as against the compensation of Rs.11,53,888/- awarded by the Tribunal along with 6% interest per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realization.

8. Hence, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is partly allowed;
ii) The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and enhanced to Rs.13,33,523/- as against Rs.11,53,888/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till its realization.
iii) Respondent No.2 is directed to pay the petitioner the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,79,635/- over and above what has been awarded by the Tribunal along with 6%
interest per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of certified copy of this order

;
iv) Draw modified award accordingly.

SD/-
